messages.subject: Re: Help with ADVI

Hi Rayleigh, the “initial variational distribution” in the error message refers to the variational distribution with parameters given by your choice of initialization (random by default, or user-specified). I suggest manually trying out different inits. Hope that helps.

best,
Dustin

std::exception::what: stan::variational::advi::adapt_eta: Cannot compute ELBO using the initial variational distribution. Your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Could you please give me advice about what settings you change to fix this issue?

Thanks.

Best,
Rayleigh

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: Help with ADVI
parts:
> So, how can I change the inits for ADVI in Cmdstan? I've already had to set the init argument for Cmdstan in order for the program to run so if we're talking about the same inits, I'm not sure I can change it. 
That's correct, the init argument for CmdStan is the init for ADVI (or whatever inference algorithm you choose). What I'm suggesting is to try other sets of initialized parameters.

> Where can I turn off optimization or sampling and still try the model using ADVI?
After compiling the model, at run time you select the inference algorithm: MCMC, variational inference, or optimization. Only one of these is `on' at a time so there's nothing to `turn off', per say.

Dustin
